test: pseudo-boundary falsification of the narrative item-initialization hypothesis
question: Is the apparent paragraph-entry transition merely an ordinary two-line fluctuation that also occurs at arbitrary positions inside paragraphs?

primary_design.pseudo_transition: all eligible internal line i -> line i+2 with i >= 1, within the same paragraph
primary_design.comparison: for paragraphs with internal pseudo-starts, compare real entry projection with the mean internal pseudo-entry projection

anti_circular_leaf_holdout.design: 5-way physical-leaf split. Learn the entry-transition direction only from training leaves, then compare real vs internal pseudo transitions on held-out leaves.

decision: The simple pseudo-boundary explanation is rejected in this development test. The two-line transition is strongly concentrated at genuine paragraph entry rather than being an ordinary within-paragraph fluctuation.
interpretation: This supports the local/directional part of P60-1: paragraph starts behave as a special state boundary. It does not establish semantics, content, plaintext, or cipher. The next falsification should ask what audited structural features carry the effect and whether it survives alternative token/unit representations.
next: Phase60B feature attribution and representation robustness for the entry-specific component.
